title: What is two fifths plus one fifth?
description: Two fifths and one fifth are drawn on rectangular strips cut into five equal parts. Both use the same fractional unit, so adding means counting the shaded parts. Keeko doubts the answer by adding the tops and adding the bottoms.
teaching_notes: One idea: when two fractions have the same fractional unit, add the number of units and keep the unit. Watch for the slip of adding the bottom numbers too.

video_script.why: A learner adds fractions with the same fractional unit by counting the units and keeping the unit as it is.
video_script.substitution: the book's own sum two fifths plus one fifth on rectangular strips
video_script.anchor: two rectangular strips, each cut into five equal parts
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko adds the tops and adds the bottoms and gets three tenths. Three tenths is smaller than two fifths alone, so the idea is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: two fifths and one fifth make three fifths

final_answer.spoken: two fifths and one fifth make three fifths

video_script.fraction_reading: two fifths, one fifth, three fifths, three tenths, four tenths
never_show: three tenths written as the sum before Keeko's doubt
maths_rules: both fractions have the same fractional unit 1/5
2/5 is 2 units of 1/5 and 1/5 is 1 unit of 1/5
slip: Keeko adds the tops and the bottoms and gets 3/10; 3/10 = 0.3 < 2/5 = 0.4, so the sum would be smaller than a part
video_script.design: Two strips cut into fifths stay on the board. The shaded parts are counted together, and the fractional unit stays one fifth.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; two strips cut into 5 equal parts, 2 parts shaded on the first strip in teal and 1 part shaded on the second in amber; the words sum? appear

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.strips: two strips cut into five equal parts appear, with two parts shaded in teal on the first and one part shaded in amber on the second
marks.ask: the words sum? appear between the strips

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book, and it asks for the sum of two fractions.
<bookmark mark='strips'/>One strip shows two fifths, and the other strip shows one fifth.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is two fifths plus one fifth?

beats.on_screen: the two strips hold still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: one strip of 5 equal parts, each part labelled 1/5; the bottom number 5 is circled with the note fractional unit

marks.unit: a strip splits into five equal parts, each labelled 1/5, and the bottom number is circled
marks.count: the shaded parts of the strip are counted one by one

narration: <bookmark mark='unit'/>Both strips are cut into five equal parts, so every part is one fifth. This is the fractional unit.
<bookmark mark='count'/>Adding two such fractions means counting all the shaded parts together.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the two fractions are two fifths and one fifth.

beats.on_screen: To find: the sum of 2/5 and 1/5
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the sum of the two fractions.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: the same fractional unit 1/5; 2/5 is 2 units and 1/5 is 1 unit

marks.same: both strips carry the label unit 1/5
marks.units: 2/5 is marked as 2 units and 1/5 as 1 unit

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>Step one, both fractions have the same fractional unit, one fifth.
<bookmark mark='units'/>Two fifths is two of these units, and one fifth is one more unit.

marks.join: the shaded parts of the second strip slide next to those of the first

narration: <bookmark mark='join'/>Step two, slide the shaded parts of the two strips together.
<bookmark mark='total'/>The total number of units is two plus one, which is three. Each unit is still one fifth.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Three units of one fifth make three fifths, so two fifths and one fifth make three fifths.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the two strips
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a bubble says add the tops and add the bottoms: 3/10; a strip of 10 equal parts with 3 shaded sits beside 2/5 and is shorter; the bubble is struck out

marks.doubt: the bubble with the wrong idea appears
marks.short: a strip of ten equal parts with three shaded sits beside two fifths and is shorter
marks.fix: the bubble is struck out and the unit 1/5 stays on the strips

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks it is three tenths, because two plus one is three and five plus five is ten.
<bookmark mark='short'/>Three tenths is smaller than the two fifths we started with, and adding cannot give less.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The pieces stay fifths. We only count how many there are.
